subject: Minimum bucket quantization and context-slicing: billing impact & proposal
messages:

To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Minimum bucket quantization and context-slicing — billing impact

Hi Kimberly / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick spike and attached a small sample (finpay-billing-sample-rows.csv) that shows what our real prompt/response sizes look like — we included both long multi-turn support tickets and short one-off lookups.

Two specific asks as we move to finalize the 12-month commit:
1) Can you confirm how the minimum billing bucket will be applied when we use context-slicing? For example: if a 40k context is sliced into three sub-requests, will each sub-request be rounded to the minimum or will rounding be applied after aggregation?
2) If we enable Redwood's low-precision quantized model variant for cheaper per-token rates, are there separate minimums/quantization-specific floors we should expect?

We flagged a couple of rows in the CSV where the user messages are tiny (10–20 tokens) and a long system prompt is reused — that is where our invoice could blow up if each call hits a per-call minimum. Can we get an example invoice line with the attached sample?

Appreciate a short writeup so our procurement team can sign off this week.

Cheers,
Lena

Subject: Re: Minimum bucket quantization and context-slicing — billing impact

Lena — thanks for the sample, and good questions. High level answers first, then I'll attach a worked example in a follow-up: 

- Aggregation: Redwood currently aggregates usage per "active conversation" window and then applies the minimum bucket at invoice line itemization. That means context-slicing itself is not automatically charged as separate full minimums if the slices are part of the same active window and we can stitch/aggregate tokens server-side. However, if slices are executed as completely independent requests (different conversation ids, no prefix reuse), they can each hit a minimum.

- Quantization variant: Quantized variants use the same billing primitives (tokens + context) but in some enterprise pilot SKUs we apply a different minimum (e.g., 500-token floor vs 1,000-token floor on standard models). That is negotiable in the deal and is why I want Karthik to weigh in — he owns the packaging concessions.

I'll prepare a two-row sample invoice showing: (a) naive per-call minimum application and (b) aggregated/windowed billing after prefix stitching. Expect that in the next message.

Best,

Subject: Re: Minimum bucket quantization and context-slicing — billing impact

Adding a few specifics from packaging/quotas side — copying Lena so you have context: 

1) Minimums & aggregation: For committed-seat/commit-tier deals we typically allow aggregation across conversation windows that share the same conversation_id for up to a 24-hour stitching window; after that we treat them as separate. If FinPay's architecture reuses conversation ids for multi-step work flows (recommended), most of your small user messages will amortize against the larger system prompt.

2) Context-slicing behavior: If you call Redwood's context-slicer helper (the service-side splitter) we maintain prefix/KV reuse where possible; when that happens we bill for the full logical context once and charge additional tokens only for non-shared segments. If you self-slice and send disjoint requests with no reuse headers, we can't stitch and you'll see multiple minimums.

3) Quantized-floor concessions: For FP-376 I can offer a concession path: 750-token floor for quantized SKUs (instead of our standard 1,000-token floor) for the first 3 months of the contract to help you evaluate cost delta. After month 3 we'll revert to agreed floor unless utilization triggers a renegotiation.

4) Example invoice: see table below (sample lines) — Kimberly will attach a mocked invoice row for your CSV.

If helpful, we can schedule a 20-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through.

- Karthik

Lena — attached are two mocked invoice lines in billing_matrix_Q1.xlsx and a short note on implementation options. Quick summary so procurement has an easy answer: 

Option A (stitching + commit): You reuse conversation_id and use Redwood server-side slicing — we aggregate and apply one minimum per stitched window. Estimated invoice for your sample: ~$1,200/mo effective (illustrative).

Option B (independent slices + no commit): Each slice may hit the 1,000-token floor -> estimated invoice becomes ~3–4x higher on low-token calls.

Concession: Karthik's offer stands: 750-token floor for quantized SKUs for first 3 months (FP-376). We'll lock that into the SOW appendix if procurement agrees.

Next steps:
- Lena: confirm if FinPay can switch to conversation_id reuse or whether your ingestion path forces independent short calls. If you can, we will draft SOW appendix with the 750-floor concession.
- Vanessa: please prepare the SOW appendix language (short clause referencing floor and reversion date).
- Karthik: please confirm the 24-hour stitching window in legal text we can share with procurement.

Happy to hop on a call — available tomorrow 10–11a PT.

Thanks,
